payload.title: Migrated claims use a guessable fencing token (claim-migrated-<id>)
payload.body: applyMigration sets claim_id = 'claim-migrated-' + task.id (git-native.ts ~1118), fully derivable from the PUBLIC task id. The fencing token is meant to be an unguessable capability proving ownership (normal claims use claim-<randomUUID>). With a guessable token, an attacker can forge ownership of a migrated task: put 'Task-Claim: claim-migrated-<id>' in a commit and check-push's fencing passes (bypassing the claim gate once enforcement is armed), and heartbeat/complete --claim accept the guessed token. Fix: use a random suffix, e.g. claim-migrated-<randomUUID>, keeping the traceable prefix but restoring unguessability. Likely warrants a short plan (security-sensitive; verify check-push + the migrated-claim tests still pass). Surfaced while giving migrated claims a lease.
